output.brief: The enrolment drop was caused mainly by the revised merit scholarship schedule, not by the Admissions Office. Yield fell from 41.8% to 34.3%. It fell by almost the same amount in early action (45.2% to 37.8%), which was handled on the old system and on time, and in regular decision (39.0% to 31.5%), which was slow. If the portal delays were the main cause, regular decision should have fallen much more. By scholarship tier, yield fell only where awards were cut (Dean's $14k to $9k, 45.2% to 31.9%; Merit $9k to $5k, 44.9% to 32.3%). It was flat where awards were unchanged (Presidential, and no-award students). Applications and admit quality rose, so a weaker pool or general demand softening doesn't fit. The regular-decision delays were real and may have cost some students, but they don't explain the drop. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in this. Whether the frozen reader posts or the portal caused the delays is unmeasured, and I haven't checked the missing-document claims. Next: don't replace the director on this basis. Take the scholarship schedule back to the finance committee, with the revenue trade-off modelled, to restore awards in the tiers that lost yield. Separately, set a turnaround target and look into the portal and staffing causes.
